verdict.rationale: Proa's own toolchain compiles components that use signals and event handlers into server-rendered HTML plus a small vanilla-JS module per island, running on a roughly 1.3 KB shared runtime. That is compiler-generated client reactivity, so developers do not hand-write update code. However, the evidence never says the emitted JS performs fine-grained or surgical DOM updates rather than re-rendering, and the compile-time template work (validation, merging static markup) concerns server HTML output. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of fine-grained/surgical DOM patching, details of how the island compiler maps signals to DOM nodes, independent or hands-on corroboration of update efficiency.

support.subject: As a developer, I can rely on a compiler to translate my components into efficient, surgical DOM updates instead of writing manual diffing code

citations.quote: Add signals and event handlers, and Proa emits the server-rendered HTML plus the JavaScript required for that island
Each hydrated RSJS island emits a small vanilla-JS module plus seed state, served with a shared runtime around 1.3 KB gzipped.
The macro validates the template at compile time, consolidates adjacent static markup, and preserves the correct escaping behavior for dynamic slots.
